'''Mete Atatüre''' (born 19 February 1975) is a Turkish physicist working on experimental [[Solid-state physics|solid-state]] [[quantum optics]], in particular on the optical control of [[Spin (physics)|spin]]-[[photon]] coupling for [[quantum network]]s as well as investigation of [[many-body physics]] in atomically-thin [[Heterojunction|heterostructures]], with the aim of developing new materials and devices for [[Quantum sensor|quantum sensing]] applications.

He currently leads the Quantum Optical Materials and Systems (QOMS) group at the [[University of Cambridge]], with about 30 PhD students and research staff.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.quantum.cam.ac.uk/mete-atature|title=Mete Atatüre Homepage}}</ref> He is also a co-founder and CSO of the spin-out ''Nu Quantum'' Ltd.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://nu-quantum.com|title=nu quantum Ltd.}}</ref> Since October 2023, he has been the Head of the [[Cavendish Laboratory]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.phy.cam.ac.uk/news/welcoming-mete-atature-new-head-department#:~:text=Commenting%20on%20his%20appointment%2C%20Mete,urge%20to%20question%20and%20challenge.|title=Professor Mete Atatüre is taking on the role of Head of Department at the Cavendish Laboratory, succeeding Professor Andy Parker.|date=2 October 2023 }}</ref>

== Biography ==

Atatüre was born in [[Kayseri]] in 1975 and completed his secondary education at the [[Gazi Anatolian High School]] in [[Ankara]] in 1992 before obtaining a Bachelor of Science degree in 1996 from the [[Bilkent University]], one of the top institutions in the country. He did his PhD at the [[Boston University]] in the United States in the Quantum Imaging Laboratory in 2002. He then moved to become a [[postdoctoral researcher]] in the Quantum Photonics Group of [[Ataç İmamoğlu]] at [[ETH Zurich]] in Switzerland where he received his [[Habilitation|Venia legendi]] for conducting long-lasting work on the full control of semiconductor [[quantum dots]], including their positioning for [[cavity QED]], the first demonstration of all-optical spin initialization and the first observation of the [[Faraday effect]] for a single spin. He joined the [[Cavendish Laboratory]] in June 2007 as a University Lecturer and Fellow of [[St John's College, Cambridge|St John's College]] and was subsequently promoted to Reader (2011) and full-professorship (2015) before becoming the head of the Cavendish Laboratory (2023).

In Cambridge, he has made groundbreaking contributions to quantum optics, including fundamentals of quantum light via [[resonance fluorescence]], quantum control of [[Atomic nucleus|nuclei]], diamond-based novel spin-photon interfaces for quantum networks, as well as the design of new functionalities from emerging classes of [[2D materials]], such as the first atomically-thin quantum [[Light-emitting diode|LED]].

== Academic and social activities ==

Atatüre is a member of the [[Institute of Physics]] in England, the [[Turkish Academy of Sciences|Science Academy of Turkey]], [[Academia Europaea]] in Europe,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Atat%C3%BCre_Mete|title=Mete Atatüre on Academia Europaea.}}</ref> and [[Optica (society)|Optica]] in the USA (formerly Optical Society of America). He was a Distinguished Visiting Professor of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] between 2010 and 2014, and he is currently a Distinguished Research Fellow of [[Sabanci University]], [[Turkey]]. He was a member of the editorial board of [[Scientific Reports]] for the period 2011–2015. He is a member of the advisory board for [[Small (journal)|Small]] since 2019 and a member of the editorial board for IoP Materials for Quantum Technology<ref>{{cite web|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/journal/2633-4356|title=IoP Materials for Quantum Technology.}}</ref> since 2023.

He is also a prominent advocator of science communication and public engagement,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CzxBqQcyIcM&ab_channel=CambridgePhilosophicalSociety|title=Professor Mete Atatüre lecturing on "Quantum Optics and Quantum Technology"|website=[[YouTube]] |date=23 April 2023 }}.</ref> with a large following on Twitter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/MeteAtature|title=@MeteAtature on Twitter.}}</ref> His noted public engagements include 6 [[TEDx]] talks on quantum physics, light, science and diversity, as well as multiple opinion pieces in published media. He is also an activist for gender equality and diversity.

He also became a popular and emblematic scientific figure in Turkey, where he makes regular appearances in—or is discussed by—the media. He was nominated Turkish man of the year for 2015 by the fashion magazine [[GQ]], who nicknamed him ""Profesör kahkaha" or "Professor Laughter" due to his friendly attitude and enthusiasm for his research".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.joh.cam.ac.uk/professor-mete-atat%C3%BCre-one-turkish-gq-magazine%E2%80%99s-men-year#:~:text=University%20of%20Cambridge-,Professor%20Mete%20Atat%C3%BCre%20is%20one%20of%20Turkish%20GQ%20Magazine's%20Men,the%20field%20of%20quantum%20physics.|title=Professor Mete Atatüre is one of Turkish GQ Magazine's Men of the Year}}</ref> He is often sighted in Cambridge University with his cat Mietzi.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/stjohnscam/status/1027128080861679616?lang=en|title=Mietziko and Mete Atatüre}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

* 2021 Elected Member of Academia Europaea (EA)
* 2020 [[Institute_of_Physics_Awards#Research_awards|Thomas Young Medal]] (IoP)<ref>{{cite web |title=Thomas Young Medal and Prize recipients |url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/silver-subject-medals/thomas-young-medal-and-prize-recipients |publisher=Institute of Physics}}</ref>
* 2020 Fellow of the [[Optical Society of America]] (OSA)
* 2020 [[European Research Council]] – Advanced Award.
* 2020 Distinguished Research Fellow, [[Sabancı University]].
* 2019 European Research Council – Proof of Concept Award.
* 2016 International Achievement Award – ForumIstanbul2023.
* 2016 Science Person of the Year – MSIC National Students' Choice Award.
* 2015 Outstanding Achievement Award – [[GQ]] Turkey Man of the Year
* 2013 European Research Council – Consolidator Award
* 2012 Elected Fellow of the [[Turkish Academy of Sciences]] (TÜBA)
* 2010 Elected Fellow of the Institute of Physics UK (IoP)
* 2010–2014 CAS Distinguished Visiting Professor – [[University of Science and Technology of China|USTC]], China
* 2007 European Research Council – Starter Award
* 2007 [[Venia legendi]] in Experimental Physics – [[ETH Zurich]]
